subject: POC kickoff + routing policy working session scheduling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: POC kickoff + routing policy working session scheduling

Hi Alice,

Great to meet you on the demo yesterday — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Per our conversation, we'd like to kick off the Acme POC next week and schedule two short sessions:

1) POC kickoff (30–45m): overview, success criteria, data/access checklist, and timeline.
2) Hands-on routing policy working session (60–90m): prompt review, model selection, fallback rules, regional tiering, and a short load test plan.

Proposed days/times (PDT):
- Tue 3/23 10:00–11:30
- Wed 3/24 14:00–15:30
- Thu 3/25 09:00–10:30

I've attached a draft POC agenda and a routing policy primer for your review. If those slots don't work, happy to find alternatives. Also looping in Dev (serving/runtime) and Laura (CS lead) to help with the working session planning.

Next step: pick one kickoff slot and one working-session slot; we'll send calendar invites and attach the runbook for the load test.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: POC_agenda.pdf, routing_policy_draft.md

Hi Marissa — thanks, this looks great.

For the kickoff, Wed 3/24 14:00 PDT works best for our team. For the hands-on working session, Thu 3/25 09:00 PDT is preferable so our infra folks can join (we have a weekly sync on Tue mornings).

A couple of asks before the working session:
- Can you confirm which models you'll recommend for a baseline (open-source options)?
- Do you have a short checklist for the load test (target QPS, sample prompts)?

Looping in our eng alias; they may propose a slightly different slot if any conflicts.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-03-18T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff + routing policy working session scheduling

Thanks — I'll put together the recommendations. Quick preview:
- Baseline models: Llama-2-13B-int8 (latency/cost balance), MPT-7B-8k (throughput-friendly), and a small 3B quantized variant for edge/low-cost fallback.
- Load test plan: start with 5 QPS sustained for 5 minutes, ramp to 25 QPS over 10 minutes, peak at 50 QPS for 5 minutes (we'll adapt based on Acme's expected concurrency). Sequence lengths: 64/256/1024 tokens samples.

I'll draft a 1-pager and share before EOD. Also adding a short checklist for pre-work (API keys, dataset samples, any latency SLOs).

— Dev
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
